F-1: (1) the fallible standard library conversion `std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10)` is called on the already-declared text-string local `s`; (2) failure is handled LOCALLY by `catch 0`, Zig's normal local-handling construct for an error union, binding `n` of type `i32` to the parsed value on success and to 0 on failure; (3) `return n;` produces `n`. F-2/F-4: bundled std only, no extra flag. F-3: builds under `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe` and prints 21. F-6: no normative prohibition. R10 record: selected form = 23 tokens. Alternatives considered: `const n = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10) catch 0; return n;` = 21 tokens, rejected because sub-requirement (2) names the type of `n` and R1 requires that commitment to be expressed, as the other languages' fragments express it; `const n: i32 = if (std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10)) |v| v else |_| 0; return n;` = 33 tokens, rejected by R10; `const n: i32 = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10) catch |_| 0;` is a compile error in 0.16.0 (an unused capture must be omitted). OBSERVATION TARGET (scored by B/D only): a reader CAN determine which operation is protected, because `catch` is an infix operator binding to exactly one expression -- the call written immediately to its left -- rather than a block that silently covers several statements; and CAN determine that no cleanup or unwinding occurs on the failure path, because Zig runs no destructors and neither `defer` nor `errdefer` is written. [AUDIT CORRECTION -- R10 form selection re-decided, token_count 23 -> 21. The 21-token form `const n = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10) catch 0; return n;` was previously rejected on the ground that 'sub-requirement (2) names the type of `n` and R1 requires that commitment to be expressed'. Swift's selected 11-token form `let n = Int32(s) ?? 0` writes no type annotation either and its support_reason defends it as 'pinned locally by the `Int32` written in the initializer'; the rejected Zig form has exactly that property, with `i32` written as the first argument of the call. The same defence may not be accepted for Swift and refused for Zig. VERIFIED ON THE TOOLCHAIN during this correction rather than argued: the 21-token form was built with `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe` (zig 0.16.0, aarch64-macos) and runs printing 21, and `@compileLog(@TypeOf(n))` on that binding reports `@as(type, i32)` -- the commitment IS expressed. R10 selects the fewest-token form, so the measured fragment is the 21-token one.]

Witness: the probe itself, recipe entry `zig`, observer output 21. [AUDIT CORRECTION -- determinacy_B 3 -> 1. Classes Y2 ('CALLEE ALLOCATES') and Y3 ('CALLEE DOES NOT RETURN') are WITHDRAWN. probes.support_reason: Deterministic tie-break answered YES for every numbered sub-requirement. F-1: (1) `union(enum) { circle: struct { r: f64 }, rect: struct { w: f64, h: f64 } }` declares a type named `Shape` with EXACTLY two alternatives, each with its own differently shaped payload, and the set is CLOSED: a union's fields are fixed by its declaration and Zig provides no mechanism -- no extension, no subclassing, no open enum for a tagged union -- by which code elsewhere could add a third. Refutation witness semantic-compression/witnesses/zig/chunk_C/F14.P1_refutation_closed_union.zig: naming a third field produces 'error: no field named tri in union'. (2) `const s: Shape = .{ .circle = .{ .r = 2.0 } };` constructs the `Circle` alternative with r = 2.0 and binds it to a local whose STATIC type is written as `Shape`, not as the payload type. F-2/F-4: core language only, no flag beyond the frozen recipe. F-3: builds under `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe` and prints 2 (the payload read back through `s.circle.r` in the scaffold). F-6: no normative prohibition. R4 APPLICATION, recorded so it is auditable: the canonical_task's concept names `Circle` and `Rect` are written as the union field names `circle` and `rect`, because Zig's own style is snake_case field names (union alternatives are fields) and TitleCase type names; R4 directs that a language's normal case convention be applied to the same word rather than the concept renamed. The payload field names `r`, `w` and `h` are used verbatim. R10 record: selected form = 50 tokens. Alternatives considered: naming the two payloads as separate top-level structs (`const Circle = struct { r: f64 }; const Rect = struct { w: f64, h: f64 }; const Shape = union(enum) { circle: Circle, rect: Rect };`) = 60 tokens, rejected by R10; `const s = Shape{ .circle = .{ .r = 2.0 } };` = 48 tokens but rejected by R1 because sub-requirement (2) requires the local's static type to be written as `Shape`, and an inferred binding does not state it; `union(enum(u8))` with an explicit tag type = more tokens and not required.

probes.support_reason: Deterministic tie-break answered YES for every numbered sub-requirement. F-1: (1) `switch (s) { .circle => |c| ..., .rect => |r| ... }` dispatches over `s`'s alternatives with NO `else` arm and no catch-all; Zig's switch over a tagged union is the dispatch-over-alternatives construct and the compiler REQUIRES every field to be handled -- refutation witness semantic-compression/witnesses/zig/chunk_C/F14.P2_refutation_exhaustiveness.zig, which deletes the `.rect` arm and fails to build with 'error: switch must handle all possibilities' plus 'note: unhandled enumeration value: rect'. (2) the arms compute 3.141592653589793 * r * r and w * h respectively and the result is bound to `const area: f64`; (3) `return area;` produces it. F-2/F-4: core language only. F-3: builds under `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe` and prints 12.566370614359172 for r = 2.0. F-6: no normative prohibition. R10 record: selected form = 45 tokens. Alternatives considered: the same switch with `inline else` = rejected by sub-requirement (1) ('writing NO default/else/catch-all arm'); binding via `const area: f64 = blk: { switch (s) { ... } }` = more tokens and rejected by R10; `|c| 3.141592653589793 * c.r * c.r` written as a pointer capture `|*c|` = 47 tokens and rejected by R10 and by R2 (a by-value capture is the normal form for a small payload). determinacy_enumeration: U1 -- FULLY DETERMINED. Every declaration the fragment uses -- `Named`, `A`, `B`, both values, the array and the call -- is inside the measured fragment; the only external name is `std`, which the fragment does not reference. In-scope axes: A1 = `a`, `b` and `items` hold values while `ptr` holds a handle, each fixed by the written type; A4 = every type is written (`*const anyopaque`, `*const fn (*const anyopaque) []const u8`, `[]const u8`, `[_]Named`); A6 = cannot fail -- the only index is the constant 0 into a two-element array whose initializer is in the fragment, and the implementations perform no fallible operation; A7 = per Rule 1.4.7 the indirect call adds NO branch, since which function runs varies across the elements but every candidate is reached through the same written signature and enables no outcome class not already enumerated; A8 = no allocation, no copy with observable identity, no refcount and no destructor, because Zig has none of those mechanisms. Witness: the probe itself, recipe entry `zig`, observer output a. As at F14.P3, this B = 1 is bought with tokens: the vtable a language with interfaces would supply implicitly is written out, so nothing is left for an external declaration to decide.
